topics.title: Stroke (BE FAST)
steps: Check Balance, Eyes, Face, Arms, Speech. Sudden trouble in any one is a warning.
Face: ask them to smile. Does one side droop? Arms: ask them to lift both. Does one drift down?
Speech: ask them to say a short sentence. Is it slurred or strange?
Note the time the signs began and tell the 911 operator.
Keep them still and comfortable. Give no food, drink or pills.
call911: Any one BE FAST sign, even if it fades
Sudden severe headache, or sudden confusion
Do not wait to see if it passes

video.title: B.E. F.A.S.T. to spot a stroke

topics.title: Dengue warning signs
steps: Fever for 2 to 7 days with body pain or headache can be dengue. Rest and sip fluids often.
Watch closely when the fever goes down, usually on day 3 to 7. This is when it can turn serious.
Go to a clinic or hospital at once for belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding gums or nose, black stool, or cold clammy skin.
Also go if the person is very sleepy, restless, or breathing fast.
Use paracetamol for fever only if a doctor agrees. Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen.
call911: Cannot stay awake, or is confused
Severe belly pain or vomiting that will not stop
Bleeding that will not stop, or vomiting blood
Cold, clammy, pale skin, or trouble breathing

topics.title: CPR (hands-only)
steps: Check the person: no answer and not breathing normally. Shout for help.
Call 911, or ask someone to call and bring an AED if there is one.
Kneel beside them. Put the heel of one hand on the middle of the chest, the other hand on top.
Push hard and fast, about 2 pushes every second, at least 5 cm deep. Let the chest come back up each time.
Keep going without stopping until help or an AED arrives, or they wake up.
call911: Always: call 911 first for anyone who will not wake and is not breathing normally

sources.label: Video: National CPR Day, Philippine Red Cross

topics.title: Choking (adult)
steps: Ask: are you choking? If they can cough, let them cough.
If they cannot cough, speak or breathe, call 911 or have someone call.
Lean them forward. Give 5 firm blows on the back between the shoulder blades.
If still stuck, give 5 quick inward and upward pushes just above the belly button.
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 belly pushes until it clears or they pass out. If they pass out, start CPR.
call911: They cannot cough, speak or breathe
They pass out
Anything is still stuck after the first round

topics.title: Heavy bleeding
steps: Call 911 if the blood is spurting, soaking through, or will not stop.
Press hard directly on the wound with a clean cloth or your gloved hand.
Keep pressing. Do not lift to peek. Add more cloth on top if it soaks through.
Once it slows, wrap a firm bandage over the pad. Not so tight that fingers turn pale or numb.
Lay the person down and keep them warm until help arrives.
call911: Blood spurts or soaks through a thick pad
Bleeding does not slow after 10 minutes of pressure
The person is pale, faint or confused
A deep wound on the head, chest or belly

topics.title: Heart attack
steps: Signs: pressure or squeezing in the chest, pain spreading to the arm, jaw or back, sweating, breathlessness, nausea.
Call 911 right away. Do not drive yourself.
Sit the person down and keep them calm and still.
If a doctor has prescribed chest-pain medicine, help them take it as directed.
If they stop responding and are not breathing normally, start CPR.
call911: Chest pain or pressure lasting more than a few minutes
Pain with sweating, breathlessness or feeling faint
Any time you are unsure: call

video.title: How to help someone experiencing a heart attack

topics.title: Burns
steps: Move away from the heat. Remove rings, watches and tight clothing near the burn before it swells.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes. Not ice.
Do not pop blisters. Do not put toothpaste, oil or butter on it.
Cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy cover, such as kitchen cling film or a clean cloth.
Keep the person warm. Give paracetamol for pain if they can normally take it.
call911: Burn bigger than the person's hand, or on the face, hands, feet or private parts
Deep burn, white, brown or charred skin
Burn from electricity or chemicals
Trouble breathing after smoke, or a burn in a baby or older adult

video.title: How do you care for a burn

topics.title: Heat stroke
steps: Signs: very hot skin, confusion, fainting, a fast pulse, headache. Sweating may stop.
Call 911. Heat stroke is an emergency.
Move them into shade or a cool room. Remove extra clothing.
Cool the body fast: wet skin with cool water and fan, or put cool wet cloths on neck, armpits and groin.
If fully awake, give small sips of cool water. Do not force fluids.
call911: Confused, very sleepy or fainting
Hot skin with no sweat
A seizure, or not getting better in 15 minutes

video.title: Mayo Clinic Minute: Heat exhaustion and heatstroke

topics.title: Seizure
steps: Stay calm and note the time it started.
Clear hard or sharp things away. Cushion their head with something soft.
Do not hold them down. Never put anything in their mouth.
When shaking stops, roll them gently onto their side.
Stay with them until fully awake. Speak softly and tell them what happened.
call911: It lasts more than 5 minutes
A second seizure follows, or they do not wake up
First seizure ever, or an injury, pregnancy, or trouble breathing afterwards

video.title: How to help someone who is having a seizure

topics.title: Fainting
steps: Lay the person flat on their back. Raise their legs about 30 cm if you can.
Loosen tight collars and belts. Give them air and space.
If they are breathing and do not wake within a minute, roll them onto their side and call 911.
When they wake, keep them lying down for a few minutes. Sit up slowly.
Give water once fully alert. Do not give food or drink to someone who is not awake.
call911: Does not wake within a minute
Chest pain, trouble breathing or a very uneven heartbeat
Injured in the fall, pregnant, or a first-ever faint in an older adult
Faints again

video.title: Helping someone who is unresponsive and breathing

topics.title: Broken bone
steps: Keep the person still. Do not try to straighten the bone.
Support the injured part in the position you found it, with rolled clothes or a pillow.
Cover any open wound with a clean cloth. Press around it, not on the bone.
Put a cold pack wrapped in cloth on it for pain and swelling.
Do not let them eat or drink in case they need an operation. Get them to a hospital.
call911: Bone through the skin, or heavy bleeding
Neck, back or head injury
Leg or hip injury they cannot move
Numb, pale or blue fingers or toes below the injury

topics.title: Drowning
steps: Shout for help and call 911. Reach or throw something that floats. Do not swim out unless trained.
Once out of the water, check if they wake and breathe normally.
If not breathing, lay them flat and start CPR. Begin with 5 rescue breaths if you know how.
Keep going until help arrives.
If they wake, lay them on their side, keep them warm, and still go to a hospital.
call911: Always call 911 for any drowning, even if they seem fine afterwards
Coughing, trouble breathing or sleepiness hours later

video.title: What to do if you suspect someone is drowning

topics.title: Snake bite
steps: Move away from the snake. Keep the person calm and still. Moving speeds the venom.
Call 911 or get to a hospital quickly.
Keep the bitten limb still and at about heart level. Take off rings and tight items.
Do not cut the bite, suck it, use a tourniquet, or apply ice.
Note what the snake looked like if safe. Do not try to catch it.
call911: Every snake bite is an emergency
Swelling spreading, drooping eyelids, trouble breathing or speaking

video.title: Every snakebite should be treated as a medical emergency

topics.title: Dog or cat bite (rabies)
steps: Wash the bite or scratch right away with soap and running water for 15 minutes.
Put on a clean cover. Do not close a deep wound tightly.
Go to an Animal Bite Treatment Centre the same day. Rabies shots work only if started early.
Do not wait to see if the animal stays healthy. Do not use herbs, garlic or stones.
Tell the doctor about the animal and any past tetanus shot.
call911: Bleeding that will not stop
Bite on the face, head or neck
Fever, confusion or fear of water after any animal bite

topics.title: Low blood sugar
steps: Signs: shaky, sweaty, hungry, pale, confused, or acting oddly. Think of it if they have diabetes.
If they can swallow safely, give fast sugar: 3 teaspoons of sugar in water, or half a glass of juice.
Wait 15 minutes. Check sugar if you have a meter.
If still low or symptoms stay, give the sugar again.
Once better, give a snack such as bread or biscuits.
call911: They are too drowsy to swallow safely
They pass out or have a seizure
Not better after two rounds of sugar

video.title: Diabetic emergency: first aid steps and key action

topics.title: Severe allergic reaction
steps: Signs: swollen lips or face, hives, wheezing, throat tightness, dizziness, or vomiting after food, a sting or medicine.
Call 911 right away.
If they have a prescribed adrenaline pen, help them use it at once, in the outer thigh.
Lay them flat with legs raised. If they struggle to breathe, let them sit up.
Stay with them. Follow the pen instructions if a second dose is needed.
call911: Trouble breathing or a tight throat
Swelling of the face or tongue
Feeling faint or collapsing

topics.title: After a fall
steps: Do not rush to pull them up. Ask where it hurts and stay calm.
Check for head, neck, back, hip or wrist pain, bleeding, or confusion.
If none of those and they feel able, help them roll to the side, then up to hands and knees and onto a sturdy chair.
If they cannot get up, keep them warm with a blanket and call for help.
Tell their doctor about any fall, even without injury.
call911: Hit the head, especially on a blood thinner
Cannot move, or hip, back or neck pain
Confused, bleeding badly, or chest pain
